class.name: TdJson
class.description: The JSON serialization of TDLib API objects is straightforward: all API objects are represented as JSON objects with the same keys as the API object field names. The object type name is stored in the special field "@type" which is optional in places where type is uniquely determined by the context. The main TDLib interface is asynchronous. To match requests with a corresponding response, the field "@extra" can be added to the request object. The corresponding response will have an "@extra" field with exactly the same value. Each returned object will have an "@client_id" field, containing the identifier of the client for which a response or an update was received. A TDLib client instance can be created through [code]TdJson.new()[/code]. Requests can be sent using [code]send[/code] and the received client identifier. New updates and responses to requests can be received through [code]receive[/code] from any thread after the first request has been sent to the client instance. This function must not be called simultaneously from two different threads. Also, note that all updates and responses to requests must be applied in the order they were received for consistency. Some TDLib requests can be executed synchronously from any thread using [code]execute[/code]. TDLib client instances are destroyed automatically after they are closed. All TDLib client instances must be closed before application termination to ensure data consistency. General pattern of usage: [codeblocks] [gdscript] var client := TdJson.new() while true: var result = client.receive(10.0) if result: # parse the result as a JSON object and process it as an incoming update or the answer to a previously sent request pass [/gdscript] [/codeblocks]

method.name: execute
method.description: Synchronously executes a TDLib request. A request can be executed synchronously, only if it is documented with "Can be called synchronously". The returned pointer can be used until the next call to [code]receive[/code] or [code]execute[/code], after which it will be deallocated by TDLib.

method.name: get_client_id
method.description: Returns client id of the session

method.name: get_tdlib_version
method.description: Returns Tdlib version. Alias to this json [codeblocks] [gdscript] { "@type": "getOption", "name": "version" } [/gdscript] [/codeblocks] Note: it doesn't start the TDLib

method.name: receive
run
method.description: Runs the TDLib client. Unnecessary if you've used `send()` before.

method.name: send
method.description: Sends request to the TDLib client. May be called from any thread.

method.name: set_log_callback
method.description:
Sets the callback that will be called when a message is added to the internal TDLib log. None of the TDLib methods can be called from the callback. Callback must contain 2 arguments: [code]verbosity_level[/code] and [code]message[/code]. By default the callback is set in private [code]set_log_message_callback[/code] function (look [url=https://github.com/Utilerain/godot-tdlib/blob/master/src/tdjson.cpp]tdjson.cpp[/url]) Pattern in usage: [codeblocks] [gdscript] func _ready(): var client := TdJson.new() client.set_log_callback(_callback)
func _callback(verbosity_level, message): # Log tracking pass [/gdscript] [/codeblocks]

method.name: set_max_verbosity_level
method.description: Sets the max verbosity level for log callbacks: - Level 0 = fatal errors - Level 1 = errors - Level 2 = warnings and debug warnings - Level 3 = informational - Level 4 = debug - Level 5 = verbose debug - Level 6+ = even more detailed logging (your own verbosity)

method.name: set_tdlib_parameters
method.description: Sets the parameters for TDLib initialization. Alias to setTdlibParameters (look [url=https://core.telegram.org/tdlib/docs/classtd_1_1td__api_1_1set_tdlib_parameters.html]setTdlibParameters[/url] class). Activates on [code]authorizationStateWaitTdlibParameters[/code] event. - [code]api_id[/code] - Application identifier for Telegram API access, which can be obtained at [url=https://my.telegram.org]https://my.telegram.org[/url]. - [code]api_hash[/code] - Application identifier hash for Telegram API access, which can be obtained at [url=https://my.telegram.org]https://my.telegram.org[/url]. - [code]application_version[/code] - Application version; must be non-empty. - [code]device_model[/code] - Model of the device the application is being run on; must be non-empty. - [code]database_directory[/code] - Path to the directory for the persistent database; by default uses user data directory ([code]"user://tdlib_data/"[/code]). - [code]use_test_dc[/code] - If true, the Telegram test environment will be used instead of the production environment. - [code]files_directory[/code] - Path to the directory for storing files; by default uses [code]database_directory[/code]. - [code]use_file_database[/code] - If true, information about downloaded and uploaded files will be saved between application restarts. - [code]use_message_database[/code] - If true, the local database will be used for storing chats and messages between application restarts. - [code]use_secret_chats[/code] - If true, support for secret chats will be enabled. - [code]system_language_code[/code] - IETF language tag of the user's operating system language; By default uses locale language of the OS. - [code]system_version[/code] - Version of the user's operating system; By default uses the version of the OS.

method.name: set_verbosity_level
method.description: Sets the verbosity level for Tdlib logs. Alias to this code: [codeblocks] [gdscript] { "@type": "setLogVerbosityLevel", "new_verbosity_level": new_verbosity_level } [/gdscript] [/codeblocks]

signal.name: request_received
signal.description: Emits when the [code]receive[/code] function will receive a response
